India’s central bank on Friday (November 13, 2026) filed a petition in the country’s apex court seeking a review of its judgment that set aside the write-off of 84.15 billion rupees ($893.8 million) of Yes Bank’s additional tier-1 bonds, the court’s website showed on Monday (November 16, 2026). An email query sent to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was not answered.
Last month, the Supreme Court had upheld a Bombay High Court ruling which had set aside the write-off of Yes Bank’s AT-1 bonds and said the write-off was impermissible.
Yes Bank, in which Japan’s Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation now holds a 24% stake, was declared insolvent six years ago; as part of a restructuring scheme, new investors were brought in and its AT-1 bonds were written off.
On Friday (November 13, 2026), Yes Bank informed exchanges that it had filed a review petition without disclosing the grounds for seeking relief.
Earlier this month, Axis Trustee Services, acting on behalf of the bondholders, filed a contempt petition in the Supreme Court alleging Yes Bank’s failure to provide a “concrete roadmap” for restoring the bonds and implementing the court’s judgment.
